findings.element: interaction-check.mjs — the `count-of-one-takes-a-plural-verb` block ("every sentence agrees with its own numeral, on screen and in the accessibility tree") and the `kpi-cards-announce-their-fact-twice` block, against the four `.kpi:not(.lead)` cards in lately.html
findings.problem: Round 2 moved the KPI row's sentence off a `.sr` text leaf and onto the group's own `aria-label`. The grammar gate was not moved with it. It still reads `el.textContent`, `el.querySelector('.sr')?.textContent` and `main p, main span, .sr` — and `.kpi .sr` is now null on all four status cards in every state, so that call passes `undefined` and returns on its first line. Nothing else in 461 assertions reads a status card's `aria-label` for content; line 1547 checks only that its length is greater than 12. On screen the numeral and its verb live in two separate elements (`1` and `has nobody's name on it`), so no string the gate ever tests contains a numeral joined to its verb. Proven by planting, in a copy of the lab outside it, three defects and re-running the gate: (a) `const phrase = word.one` — the surface then reads "3 hasn't moved in a fortnight", "2 is past the day it was due", "0 is waiting on something else" and speaks "3 jobs is past the day it was due, of 9 jobs open", a literal hit for the block's own `/\bjobs\s+(has|is|was)\b/` — 461 assertions, 0 failing; (b) `const phrase = word.many` — "1 job have nobody's name on them" — 461 assertions, 0 failing; (c) the denominator falsified to `D.open + 3`, so every card is announced "of 12 jobs open" beside a plate that reads 9 — 461 assertions, 0 failing. Replacing all four names with the string "aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa" fails exactly one assertion, and only because of the separate `not available` check.
findings.consequence: The entire spoken sentence of the five-card row — its numeral, its verb agreement and its shared denominator — is unguarded. A screen-reader user is the only reader who hears the denominator at all, and the protected shared-nine contract can be wrong in their ear, in every state, with both gates green. Two of the three planted defects are also visible on screen. This is the class the library names as costing the credibility of the whole product, and it is the class this gate believes it is watching.
findings.fix: In the `count-of-one-takes-a-plural-verb` block, replace `check(el.querySelector('.sr')?.textContent, 'card name')` with a parse of the card's own accessible name, and assert it against the card's rendered numeral: for each `.kpi:not(.lead)`, read `name = card.getAttribute('aria-label')` and `shown = card.querySelector('.t-num').textContent.trim()`. When `shown !== '—'`, assert `name` begins with exactly `${shown} job ` when `shown === '1'` and `${shown} jobs ` otherwise; assert `check(name, 'card name')` for the two existing verb-agreement patterns; and assert `name` ends with `of ${window.LATELY_FIXTURE.bound.openCount === 1 ? '1 job' : window.LATELY_FIXTURE.bound.openCount + ' jobs'} open`. When `shown === '—'`, assert `/not available/i.test(name)` and that `name` contains no digit. Add the same numeral-and-verb parse to the visible pair by joining the card's `.t-num` and `.t-small` text with a single space before running `check`, so the on-screen half is no longer split across two elements the regex can never see. Write it first, plant `const phrase = word.one`, watch all four state assertions fail, then restore.
findings.assertion: For every state in full, partial, quiet, first-run: for each `.kpi:not(.lead)`, the card's `aria-label` starts with its own rendered `.t-num` value followed by `job` when that value is 1 and `jobs` otherwise, contains neither `/\bjobs\s+(has|is|was)\b/` nor `/\b1 job\s+(have|are|were|haven't|aren't)\b/`, and ends with `of <LATELY_FIXTURE.bound.openCount> job(s) open` — unless the card's numeral is an em dash, in which case the name matches /not available/i and holds no digit. The same two verb patterns are run against `.t-num` and `.t-small` joined by a space. Planting `const phrase = word.one` in lately.html must fail this in all four states; the gate today passes 461/461 with that plant in place.

findings.element: `.bar-val` ("12 so far") in the twelve-week chart, and its solo twin in state=first-run — lately.html, `.bar-val` rule and the `@keyframes grow` choreography
findings.problem: `.bar-val` carries no animation. It is positioned from `--h` at first paint, so at `?motion=play` it is at opacity 1, in its final place, from frame one — while the column it labels is still flat on the baseline. Driven at 1440, state=full: at t=100ms the label's top is 290px and its bar's top is 479px (the baseline) at 0px height; at 340ms and 620ms the bar is still 0px and the label is still at 283px; the bar first shows height at 780ms (28.4px) and only reaches full at ~1280ms. So for the first ~780ms of a 1.7s entrance the one indigo mark in movement one hangs at the top of an empty plot with nothing beneath it. In state=first-run the plot holds that single column and nothing else, so for the first ~340ms the chart is a floating indigo "12 so far" over blank white — the first frame a new customer sees. The rest of the choreography is disciplined about exactly this: `.record-tag` is held to 1.5s so the previous-best tag arrives after its own rule draws at 1.1s. The live week's value was left out of that ordering.
findings.consequence: The surface's single memorable image — the hatched, open-topped current week with its indigo "so far" — assembles backwards every time the page is opened at full speed. For most of a second the reader sees a value label with no mark under it, which is the orphaned-label class round 1 removed twice elsewhere, and on a slow device or a paused frame it reads as a chart that failed to draw. It costs the one moment on this page that was designed to feel like something.
findings.fix: Emit `--i` on the value label as well as on the bar — in `chart()`, change the live column's label to `style="--h:${pct(w.v, max)};--i:${i}"`, and in the first-run solo plot to `style="--h:100;--i:0"` — then add, beside the existing `.bar-val` rule in lately.html: `.bar-val { animation: rise 0.35s var(--ease) backwards; animation-delay: calc(var(--i) * 40ms + 800ms); }`. That places the label 460ms after its own column starts growing and 40ms before it finishes, so it lands as the mark completes, in the same order the previous-best tag already follows its rule. No new colour, weight or object. `[data-motion="settled"]`, `prefers-reduced-motion` and `[data-state="loading"]` already zero every delay and animation, so no graded frame changes.
findings.assertion: In state=full and state=first-run at `?motion=play`, sampled 300ms after `window.__LATELY_READY`: the last `.colw`'s `.bar` has a rendered height under 10% of the `.plot` height AND its sibling `.bar-val` has computed opacity under 0.1. Sampled again at 1600ms: the bar's rendered height is within 1px of its settled height AND `.bar-val` opacity is 1. Today the 300ms sample reads bar height 0px with label opacity 1.

findings.element: state=error — the `<div role="alert">` wrapping `#mError` and its paragraph inside `.center`
findings.problem: `.center` is a column flex with `gap: var(--gap-line)`, and `h1..h4, p { margin: 0 }`. In the empty and quiet states the heading and its paragraph are direct children of `.center`, so the rung applies. In the error state they were wrapped in a `role="alert"` div — the round 1 fix for terminal states announcing nothing — and that div is now the single flex child. It takes the gap for itself and its two children get none. Measured from rendered boxes at 1440 and at 390, state=error: gap from the bottom of "Tasks did not answer" to the top of "This reading needs the Tasks records..." is **0.0px**. The same measurement is 16.0px in state=empty and 16.0px in state=quiet. The button below still gets 24px in all three, so the error card's internal rhythm reads 0 / 24 where its siblings read 16 / 24. This is the round 1 margin fix undone in the one state by the round 1 accessibility fix — the file's own comment says the ladder is the only thing that sets vertical space here.
findings.consequence: The state a person meets when something has gone wrong is the one state composed carelessly: a 26px semibold heading collides with the 15px sentence explaining it, with only leading between them, at every width. It is a small thing that lands at the exact moment the product most needs to look in control, and it makes the error card read as unfinished beside the empty card it sits next to in any state deck.
findings.fix: Add one rule beside `.center` in lately.html: `.center > [role="alert"] { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: var(--gap-line); }`. The alert div then propagates the same rung its siblings get, the announcement is unchanged, and no other state is touched.
findings.assertion: For states error, empty and quiet at 1440 and 390: the vertical gap between the bottom of the state's `.center` heading (`#mError`, `#mEmpty`, or the `.t-head`) and the top of the paragraph that immediately follows it equals the computed `row-gap` of the enclosing `.center`, within 0.5px, measured from `getBoundingClientRect()`. Today error reads 0.0px against a 16px row-gap while empty and quiet read 16.0px.

findings.element: state=partial — the `What's quietly slipping` band-head label and the lead card's `.sr` sentence in `leadKpi()`
findings.problem: The shared denominator is a protected object: all five cards read the same 9. In state=partial one of the five deliberately does not — the overdue card renders an em dash, the words "Not available", and the accessible name "Jobs past the day they were due: not available, because Timeline did not answer". The two sentences that state the contract were not qualified for that state. The band-head still prints `All five counted out of 9`, and the lead card still speaks, verbatim, `Every card in this row is counted out of these 9 open jobs.` Driven at 1440 with `?state=partial`, both strings are present in the same row as the card that carries no count. The visible label is arguable — a scanner is corrected by the dash beside it — but the spoken sentence is a present-tense universal ("Every card ... is counted") delivered to the one reader who cannot see the dash correcting it, and it is heard before the card that contradicts it.
findings.consequence: A screen-reader user in the degraded state is told the row's denominator applies to every card, then hears one card say it has no answer. The honest-degradation contract is the thing this state exists to demonstrate, and the sentence that frames it overstates in exactly the state built to prove it. A header that disagrees with its own marks is the paid-for class the library names as spending the credibility of the whole product.
findings.fix: Pass the flag through: change `leadKpi(0)` to `leadKpi(0, partial)` in `movementTwo`, change the signature to `leadKpi(i, partial = false)`, and make the `.sr` line read `${partial ? "Every card in this row that has an answer is counted out of these" : "Every card in this row is counted out of these"} ${plural(D.open, "open job", "open jobs")}.` In the same function, change the band-head label to `${partial ? "Four counted out of" : "All five counted out of"} ${D.open}`. No metric changes, no card changes, no new object.
findings.assertion: In state=partial: if any `.kpi` in the row has an `aria-label` matching /not available/i, then no text or accessible name in that band may match `/^All five counted out of/` or `/Every card in this row is counted out of/`; the band-head label matches `/^Four counted out of \d+$/` and the lead card's `.sr` matches `/that has an answer is counted out of/`. In state=full both must still read `All five counted out of <open>` and `Every card in this row is counted out of these <open> open jobs.`

findings.element: `.ghost-say .t-head` — "Open work over time — the chart that would go here", capped at `max-width: 34ch`
findings.problem: The 34ch cap resolves to 464.44px, which lands one word short of the sentence. Measured by walking the text node's client rects at 390, 768, 900, 1024, 1280 and 1440: at every width from 768 up the headline breaks as "Open work over time — the chart that would go" / "here", leaving the single word that does the pointing alone on line two, centred, in the largest bold type in the lower half of the page. Only at 390, where the cap stops binding and the container is 340px, does it break well ("...the chart" / "that would go here"). So the one break that reads correctly is the phone, and every desk and tablet width the product ships orphans the word.
findings.consequence: The drawn-but-empty plot is the boldest idea on this surface and the caption is its whole payload. A stranded final word is the one place the typography looks unconsidered, and it is on the object a discerning reader will remember the product by. It costs nothing in comprehension and a real amount in whether this looks like months of iteration.
findings.fix: Add `text-wrap: balance;` to the `.ghost-say .t-head` rule in lately.html and keep the 34ch cap. Verified in chromium at 390, 768, 1280 and 1440: it produces the identical, balanced break "Open work over time — the" / "chart that would go here" at every one of them, keeping the clause that carries the idea intact on the second line. One declaration, no magic number, no new colour or weight, and no change to any other object.
findings.assertion: For each viewport in 390, 768, 900, 1280 and 1440: `.ghost-say .t-head` renders on no more than two lines, and its final line contains at least two words. Today the final line is the single word `here` at 768, 900, 1024, 1280 and 1440.

biggestWin: Fix the entrance so the live week's value arrives with its own column instead of ~780ms before it. The hatched, open-topped current week under an indigo "12 so far" is the single memorable image this surface owns — it is what a stranger would describe afterwards, and it is the only place the product makes an argument in a mark rather than a sentence. Today that image assembles backwards on every load: the label is already at the top of the plot at 100ms, the column is still 0px at 620ms, and the two only agree at 1280ms. Everything else in the choreography is ordered around the reading; this one object is not, and it is the object worth ordering most. One inline `--i` and one animation rule buys back the moment the whole page is built to deliver.
